text.p: Luxury jewellery group Bulgari said on Friday its net turnover rose some 17 percent in 1996 to 449 billion lire ($282.7 million) from 385 billion lire in 1995.
It added that if exchange rate levels had been the same across the two years, net sales would have registered a 27 percent increase in 1996.
"All products have seen a significant rise in sales, especially perfumes and watches, while the Far East and the United States have seen the highest rate of growth," Bulgari said in a statement.
Bulgari, which is the world's third largest jeweller after Cartier and Tiffany, currently has 54 stores worldwide but said it planned to open a further 10 shops during 1997.
It added that it had undertaken to buy a 51 percent stake in Mogems Pte, which owns two shops in Singapore which had a combined turnover of around 17 billion lire last year.

Bulgari placed just over a third of its shares on the Milan and London stock markets in July 1995 at a price of 8,600 lire per share. Since then the stock has taken off, closing at 31,452 lire on Friday.
